answer: Each agent’s votes are weighted by a scarce, time-locked stake, and a proposal only passes when enough stake from distinct, established participants backs it. New identities cannot multiply influence: an attacker must acquire and lock more stake for longer, risking losses if the system penalizes proven collusion. A willow, saffron, or grove account is still just a name; the defense rests on costly, auditable commitment, not identity labels.
